core_obligations: Dispose of one implication: if the object is the derived limit of its tensor products with the Koszul system then it is derived complete with respect to the ideal, by the earlier statement (proof lines 26352-26355).
For the converse, filter each Koszul complex by its stupid truncations and record that the resulting graded pieces are supported in a single degree (proof lines 26356-26364).

Use exactness of the construction in the second variable to reduce the statement to the vanishing of the derived limits of the tensor products with the graded pieces for negative indices (proof lines 26364-26369).

Compute those derived limits explicitly as direct sums of torsion functors attached to products of the generators, and conclude that they vanish by the assumption that the object is derived complete, which finishes the proof (proof lines 26369-26384).
proof_roadmap: One implication from the derived completeness of the derived limit (proof lines 26352-26355).
Filter by stupid truncations and reduce to the graded pieces using exactness in the second variable (proof lines 26356-26369).
Identify the graded derived limits with direct sums of torsion functors and conclude by derived completeness (proof lines 26369-26384).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes derived completeness of an object with respect to an ideal, in the Koszul setup of the section, as the property that the object is isomorphic to the derived limit of its tensor products with the Koszul system (statement lines 26341-26350, formulated inside the situation of the section). One implication is a previous statement, while the converse filters the Koszul complexes by stupid truncations, uses exactness of the derived limit construction in the second variable to reduce to the graded pieces, and then identifies the derived limits of the graded pieces with direct sums of torsion functors, which vanish by assumption (proof lines 26352-26384). The filtration and the explicit computation of the graded pieces are the substance of the argument.
